test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 24 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To value the rich heritage of our composite ​culture
To not indulge in corrupt practices
To respect freedom of speech of others

solution:
The correct answer is __**To value the rich heritage of our composite culture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** were introduced in the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**. They are enshrined in **Article 51A**.
 
• One of the Fundamental Duties includes the obligation to **value and preserve the rich heritage of India’s composite culture**. This duty aims to inspire citizens to protect and promote India's diverse cultural legacy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are applicable to **all Indian citizens**, and while they are not enforceable by law, they serve as a moral obligation to uphold the spirit of the Constitution.
 
• The statement “To value the rich heritage of our composite culture” is directly mentioned in **Article 51A(f)**, making it a part of the Fundamental Duties.
 
• Other duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, and striving for excellence, all of which aim to foster a sense of responsibility among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties Overview:**

 
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties were inspired by the **Constitution of the USSR** and aim to promote patriotism and strengthen the unity of the nation.
 
• While these duties are non-justiciable, they complement Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** is also known as the “Mini Constitution” due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Besides introducing Fundamental Duties, it emphasized the importance of Directive Principles and strengthened the powers of the central government.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Composite Culture:**
 
 
• India is known for its **diverse culture and heritage**, including monuments, art forms, languages, festivals, and traditions.
 
• The duty to preserve this heritage encourages citizens to actively participate in cultural preservation initiatives such as protecting historical sites and promoting cultural awareness.
 
• Examples include the **Clean India Campaign** to preserve heritage sites and cultural festivals such as **Surajkund Mela** and **International Yoga Day**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by the judiciary and provide protection to individuals, **Fundamental Duties** serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• Both aim to uphold the democratic framework of India and ensure the holistic development of society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:** **Article 51A** lists duties such as respecting the Constitution, cherishing national heritage, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.
 
• **Enforcement:** While Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable, several initiatives like cultural education programs and civic awareness campaigns promote adherence.
 
• **Global Context:** Countries like **Japan** and **Russia** also emphasize citizen duties in their constitutions, highlighting the universal importance of moral obligations.
 
• **Civic Awareness:** Schools and colleges in India conduct programs to instill the importance of Fundamental Duties among students.
